description: Shared accept/reject cases for the strict-JSON twins: web/src/actions/strictJson.ts (parseStrictJson) and src/frisket/ops/api_call_request.py (strict_json_loads). Both are deliberately independent implementations of the same rule set (reject duplicate object keys, comparing DECODED key strings not source spelling; reject non-finite numbers) and carry no shared runtime code — this fixture is the parity guard. Consumed by web/tests/unit/strictJson.test.ts and tests/ops/test_strict_json_fixture.py. `expect` is 'accept' or 'reject'; 'reason' categorizes the rejection (informational only — the two implementations raise different exception types/messages).

cases.name: big_integer
cases.note: Structurally accepted by both; Python keeps arbitrary precision while JS numbers lose precision above 2^53 (no rejection either side).

cases.name: duplicate_key_via_unicode_escape_spelling
cases.note: Both implementations compare DECODED key strings, not source spelling: \u006e decodes to 'n', so this collides with the literal 'name' key.
